comparison: Perfect agreement on YAP/TAZ-independent mechanism (C3, C13-C17, C24-C27). Both evaluations treat this as a central, novel finding with strong experimental support from co-IP and knockdown experiments. OpenEval cites specific figures; peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as a key discovery.

Perfect agreement on in vitro EP300 inhibitor efficacy (C5, C57-C62). Both evaluations support the differential effect on fusion proteins versus YAP5SA. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and triplicate experiments; peer reviewers confirm the therapeutic potential and specificity.

Perfect agreement on in vivo therapeutic efficacy (C6, C63-C69). Both evaluations affirm tumor growth inhibition, reduced Ki67 staining, and decreased target gene expression with A485 treatment. OpenEval details statistical significance; peer reviewers confirm therapeutic implications for rhabdomyosarcoma treatment.

Strong agreement on transcriptional activation (C2, C7, C8, C12). Both evaluations support TEAD target gene upregulation with high statistical significance. OpenEval includes C74 and emphasizes luciferase and RNA-seq data; peer reviewers focus on the convincing nature of transcriptional signatures.

Strong agreement on genomic occupancy and TEAD motif enrichment (C28-C30, C32-C34, C36). Both evaluations support the integrated ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN findings. OpenEval includes C31 and C35; peer reviewer notes some complexity in transcriptional overlap between fusion proteins and YAP5SA in 293T cells.

Strong agreement on EP300 recruitment mechanism (C4, C37-C38, C45-C48, C50-C51, C53). Both evaluations affirm BioID proteomics and co-IP data showing specific EP300 association. OpenEval includes additional claims (C41, C55-C56); peer reviewers treat this as a key mechanistic discovery supporting the overall model.

Strong agreement on requirement for both fusion parts (C9, C10, C11). Both evaluations support deletion construct and proliferation data. OpenEval includes C78 and emphasizes dose-response data; peer reviewer notes potential limitation of overexpression approaches not fully reflecting pathological conditions.

Strong agreement on CP1 resistance and TEAD dependence (C19-C23). Both evaluations support differential sensitivity to TEAD inhibition. OpenEval includes C84-C85 and emphasizes therapeutic implications; peer reviewers note this is informative about fusion protein mechanisms and targeting strategies.

Agreement on motif enrichment analysis (C42, C49). Both evaluations support CREB motif findings. OpenEval includes C52 and discusses CREB3 locus as control; peer reviewers implicitly accept this as supporting evidence for EP300 recruitment without raising concerns.

Agreement on NCOA2 domain requirement for EP300 binding (C55, C56). Both evaluations support co-IP data showing loss of EP300 association with NCOA2 deletion mutants. OpenEval groups this with broader EP300 recruitment claims; peer reviewers specifically validate functional importance of NCOA2 domain.

Agreement on background context and fusion protein characterization (C1, C96, C97, C110). Both evaluations accept established literature and structural descriptions. OpenEval includes C111 and emphasizes prior publications; peer reviewers treat this as uncontested background for the study.

Agreement on structural characterization (C92-C95). Both evaluations support protein structure descriptions as fundamental to understanding fusion function. OpenEval emphasizes this as essential for interpreting functional data; peer reviewers accept this as part of the valuable study description.

OpenEval finds the major conceptual conclusion (C70-C71, C79-C81) about YAP/TAZ-independent TEAD activation and EP300-dependent mechanism well-supported by combined evidence. No corresponding isolated peer review evaluation, though this conclusion is implicit in peer acceptance of individual findings (R2, R3, R4, R5).

OpenEval supports claims about therapeutic targeting challenges and future research needs (C82-C83, C86-C87) based on prior literature and CP1 resistance data. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressing these forward-looking therapeutic strategy claims.

OpenEval rates VGLL2-CITED2 fusion speculation (C88-C89) as UNCERTAIN, noting C89 lacks direct experimental validation despite reasonable hypothesis. No corresponding peer review evaluation addressing this specific fusion variant or its potential mechanism.

OpenEval rates broader therapeutic applicability claims (C90-C91) as UNCERTAIN, noting extension to other tumor types lacks direct experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressing therapeutic generalization beyond scRMS models tested.

OpenEval supports background claims about EP300 function and histone acetylation (C39-C40, C43-C44) as well-established from prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation, as these are accepted background facts providing mechanistic context.

OpenEval supports structural and mechanistic background claims (C72-C73, C75-C77) based on protein structure data and established VGLL4/NCOA function. No corresponding peer review evaluation, as these provide uncontested mechanistic context.

OpenEval supports extensive background claims about Hippo pathway and YAP/TAZ biology (C98-C109) based on prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation, as these establish accepted scientific foundation rather than novel findings requiring evaluation.
